deficiencies.description: The rewrite states that the stained slice through a tumour 'illustrates this', creating an unsourced link back to the explantation of tumours mentioned in the preceding sentence. The lecturer does not state that the slice illustrates tumour explantation.
deficiencies.sourcePassage: often they will explant the tumor. Here you're looking at a slice through a tumor and a stain to look at the morphology.

considerations.sourcePassage: Primary cells really don't grow in culture.
considerations.reason: The omission of 'really' removes colloquial emphasis rather than a scientific hedge, which is an allowed stylistic change.

considerations.sourcePassage: throw it into a plastic tissue culture dish
considerations.reason: Changing 'throw it into' to 'placed in' is an allowed stylistic change of informal phrasing to textbook prose.

considerations.sourcePassage: Whoops, I forgot to start my clock. Okay.
considerations.reason: This is a dropped remark to the audience / spoken filler, which is an allowed omission.

considerations.sourcePassage: things like the stroma and other things
considerations.reason: Rewording 'other things' to 'other components' is an allowed stylistic change that preserves the original meaning.

considerations.sourcePassage: So when HeLa cells, which were the first tumor cells to grow in culture, did that, this was very much a surprise.
considerations.reason: The rewrite rephrases the sentence without 'did that' while faithfully conveying that HeLa cells growing in culture was a surprise.
